segments.narration: The Moon is falling right now — it has been falling for billions of years — and yet it never gets any closer. That is the paradox at the heart of gravity.
Every two objects in the universe pull on each other — not just planets. Right now, your coffee cup is tugging on the Earth, ever so slightly, and the Earth tugs back with exactly the same force.
The pull gets stronger with more mass — a heavier object has a longer arrow downward. But move that object farther away, and the arrow shrinks. Distance weakens the grip.

Narrate: gravity is not a special planetary power — it is the same tug, acting at every scale, from coffee cups to galaxies. Restore the Moon diagram from the thumbnail to full size. Redraw the Moon's curved falling path prominently. Add a small dot on Earth's surface with an identical curving arc — a thrown ball — so both arcs look the same shape. Narrate: the ball and the Moon are doing the same thing. That is gravity.
